title: A GPC3-targeted MOF-818 nanoplatform for synergistic hepatocellular carcinoma therapy: integrating traditional Chinese medicine and nanotechnology
content: Precision therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is challenging due to inadequate tumor targeting, frequent drug resistance, and severe systemic toxicity. In this study, we have constructed a Glypican-3 (GPC3)-targeted metal organic framework (MOF-818)-based multifunctional nanoplatform MOF-818@ICA@GOx/PDA/GPC3 (MIGG) that is co-loaded with glucose oxidase (GOx) and icariin to enable a synergistic starvation/oxidative therapy and apoptosis induction in HCC. The MIGG actively accumulates in tumor tissues via anti-GPC3 antibody-mediated targeting, exploiting the robust glycolytic metabolism of cancer cells to generate H2O2in situ, inducing oxidative DNA damage. MIGG treatment induces apoptosis and alters the expression of genes associated with cellular stress and apoptosis. In vitro studies have demonstrated that the MIGG exhibits selective uptake and concentration-/time-dependent cytotoxicity with respect to GPC3-positive HCC cells, accompanied by a potent reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst and apoptosis. Transcriptomic analysis reveals upregulation of stress-response genes and enrichment of p53-associated and apoptosis-related gene sets. In an orthotopic HCC mouse model, the MIGG markedly suppressed tumor growth, improving liver function, inducing tumor necrosis and apoptosis, and remodeling the tumor microenvironment. This study establishes the MIGG as a precision therapeutic strategy that integrates traditional Chinese medicine with nanotechnology, offering a promising synergistic approach for HCC with significant clinical translation potential.
